\paragraph{Architectural implications.}
Attention ablation at L1 confirms functional specialization: removing instruction attention does not disrupt classification but redistributes attention to image tokens, recovering action encoding ($R^2$ $+46\%$, $p < 0.0001$), with deep layers unaffected ($|\Delta R^2| < 0.01$).
This dissociation confirms genuine head specialization while cautioning against interpreting attention as a causal bottleneck.

\paragraph{Limitations and scope.}
We study OpenVLA-7B on LIBERO; generalization to other VLAs (e.g., RT-2~\cite{brohan2023_rt2}, $\pi_0$~\cite{black2024_pi0}) remains open.
Token-level specialization generalizes via the causal mask; routing may be Llama-2-specific.
Encoder rankings and per-layer profiles are metric-dependent: RSA yields an inverted-U and ranks DINOv2 highest, while CKA shows monotonic profiles and different orderings (Appendix~\ref{sec:cka_appendix}); the $R^2$ inverted-U (L8--L13 peak) provides metric-independent evidence.
The DINOv2 advantage reflects pre-fusion geometry within a frozen encoder; end-to-end fine-tuning may alter this.
The L1 ablation uses 5 demonstrations per task (full-scale replication in progress); analyses are post-hoc (Appendix~\ref{sec:metric_sensitivity_appendix}).
Code will be released upon acceptance.
